issue.title: [Bug] Linux/Guix: startup writes a desktop entry whose Exec is the loader (os.Executable() under a wrapper), and always overwrites a packaged one
issue.body:
Environment: Guix System, `magpie-linux-amd64` 0.1.1203.

Guix cannot run the release binary directly — every library lives at its own
`/gnu/store/...` path — so the packaged launcher is a wrapper that execs

    ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 --argv0 <real> --library-path <libs> <real>

which is the same shape as the Flatpak case fixed in #849: the desktop entry
has to come from the package, because the executable path magpie can see is
not launchable as-is.

Two places still write that path:

1. The scheme registration that #849 gated on `FLATPAK_ID` writes
   `$XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/magpie.desktop` with `Exec=<os.Executable()> %u`.
   Under the loader, `/proc/self/exe` is
   `/gnu/store/...-glibc-2.41/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`, so the entry lands as

   ```
   Exec=/gnu/store/...-glibc-2.41/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 %u
   ```

   which cannot start magpie. `XDG_DATA_HOME` outranks `XDG_DATA_DIRS`, so it
   shadows the packaged entry and the menu item stops working. Note `argv[0]`
   is already the correct absolute path in this setup (the launcher passes it
   with `--argv0`), and the write is unconditional — every start rewrites the
   file, so there is no way to pre-seed a working one (a read-only 0444 file
   is currently the only thing that survives).

2. The WebKit data directory is keyed the same way, so GUI state lands in
   `~/.local/share/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2/` (`hsts-storage.sqlite`,
   `localstorage/`, `mediakeys/`) instead of `~/.local/share/magpie/`.

Would you take a generic gate for installs the package manager owns instead
of the Flatpak-specific check — for example honoring an environment variable
(`MAGPIE_NO_DESKTOP_REGISTRATION=1` or similar) the same way `FLATPAK_ID` is
honored — and preferring an absolute `argv[0]` over `/proc/self/exe` for both
the `Exec=` line and the WebKit data-dir name? That would let Guix (and
anything packaged similarly) ship a working entry while magpie leaves the
file alone.

Repro (Guix): run the release binary via
`ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 --argv0 <real> --library-path <libs> <real>`, then read
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/applications/magpie.desktop`.

Happy to test a fix on Guix.

comments.body:
Same root cause as this issue, on NixOS, with a crash attached.

## Environment

- NixOS 26.11 (nixos-unstable), x86_64-linux, niri + Noctalia
- magpie 0.1.2591 / `unstable-2026-11-01` (source `bd5152c`), packaged by the `sugar/magpie` flake
- packaged with `wrapGAppsHook3`, GTK 3.24.52, WebKitGTK 4.1

The Nix package layout is:

```text
bin/magpie-app            # wrapper: sets XDG_DATA_DIRS, including gtk3's private GSettings schemas
bin/.magpie-app-wrapped   # real binary
```

## What happens

Both generated entries use `os.Executable()`, so they point at the real binary and bypass the wrapper:

```ini
# ~/.config/autostart/magpie.desktop
Exec="/nix/store/.../bin/.magpie-app-wrapped" tray

# ~/.local/share/applications/magpie.desktop
Exec=/nix/store/.../bin/.magpie-app-wrapped %u
```

Launched from either entry, the process's `XDG_DATA_DIRS` contains `gsettings-desktop-schemas` but not the GTK3 schema directory. `org.gtk.Settings.FileChooser.gschema.xml` exists only in the GTK3 package path. Opening any file chooser (Settings → Sync & Backup → Import → Choose) aborts:

```text
No GSettings schemas are installed on the system
SIGABRT: abort
signal arrived during cgo execution
```

The backup import never runs; the app exits as soon as the dialog is used. Launching `magpie-app` from a terminal works because the wrapper environment is present. This is not specific to backup import; any GTK file chooser hits it.

## Suggested fix

Let the packager provide the launch path, as requested here:

- Honor an environment variable such as `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` in `internal/autostart/autostart.go` (`self()`) and `internal/gui/scheme_linux.go` (`registerScheme()`) before `os.Executable()`.
- When that variable is set, return it directly; do not run `filepath.EvalSymlinks` on it, or the wrapper path can be resolved back to the real binary.
- Alternatively, prefer an absolute `argv[0]` when it names the launcher.
- Keep `keepWebData()` on the real executable, since it uses the binary name for the WebKit data directory.

The Nix `wrapGAppsHook3` wrapper can then set `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE="$out/bin/magpie-app"` and both generated entries remain launchable.

### Conclusion

Reproduced the wrapper path on Windows/amd64 at `d29f02d6501a71d45661a36354afd950c2277c6b` (`v0.1.2734`) on 2026-11-02. The narrow fix is to let a packager supply the launcher in `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE`; both generated autostart and scheme entries can then name the wrapper without resolving it back to the real binary.

### Evidence

Before the change, `self()` ignored `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` and returned the resolved test executable instead of `/nix/store/example/bin/magpie app`. After the change, the autostart test returns the packager value exactly, without `EvalSymlinks`.

The same input now produces a scheme entry with:

```ini
Exec="/nix/store/example/bin/magpie app" %u
```

The quoting matters because a wrapper path can contain spaces. With the variable unset, `TestSet`, the existing `registerScheme` cases, and `keepWebData()` keep their previous code paths. `TestSelfUsesPackagerExecutable` failed on the old code and passed after the change; the autostart regression set passed. `gofmt`, `git diff --check`, Linux/Windows vet, Windows/Linux/macOS builds, and a Linux test-binary compile for `internal/gui` and `internal/autostart` passed.

### Boundary

This is opt-in for packagers. `APPIMAGE`, the Flatpak early return, the default `os.Executable()` path, and the WebKit data-directory choice are unchanged. `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` is used as written, including a relative or nonexistent path; validating the launcher remains the packager's responsibility.

### Gap

Not tried: a real NixOS `wrapGAppsHook3` or Guix loader session, a real GNOME/KDE/niri desktop parsing the quoted `Exec`, and a file chooser launched from the generated entry. The Linux scheme test was cross-compiled but not executed on Windows. A literal `%` in the wrapper path still needs desktop-entry escaping and is outside this change.

### Action

A local patch is ready. If `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` is the contract you want, I can paste the diff and the test changes here for review.

Delivered the `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` contract HoronLee asked for and Edward4226's patch-in-waiting describes — the same shape both named, so the two patches are interchangeable; this one is up for review either way.

**Root cause.** Both generated entries take the program from `os.Executable()` — on Linux `/proc/self/exe`. Behind a packager's launcher that is the binary inside the launcher, not the launcher: under Guix's `ld-linux` wrapper it is the loader itself (the entry cannot start anything), and under NixOS's `wrapGAppsHook` wrapper it is `bin/.magpie-app-wrapped`, so the entry bypasses the wrapper's `XDG_DATA_DIRS` and a GTK file chooser aborts with "No GSettings schemas are installed".

**Branch** (`fix/1747-linux-guix-startup-writes-a`, head `d0409dbbb4741859732026a268c61aab1a870c1f`):

- `internal/autostart/autostart.go` `self()`: `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE`, set by the packager, names the program the login record starts. Used as written — no `EvalSymlinks`, which would resolve the wrapper back to the binary inside — checked before `APPIMAGE`, as the packager's explicit word.
- `internal/gui/scheme_linux.go` `registerScheme()`: the same variable names the program the `magpie://` entry starts (`launcherOf`), after the `FLATPAK_ID` gate, which still wins. The `Exec=` key now quotes a path with a space in it, escaped as the desktop-entry spec takes (`execKey`) — the existing unquoted form is byte-identical for space-free paths, so entries already written are still left alone.
- `keepWebData()` untouched, as HoronLee suggested: the WebKit data folder is keyed on the executable, not the launcher (and on current main it already lives under `~/.local/share/magpie` by `programName`, which covers the loader-named folder from the original report).

A Nix package can now set `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE="$out/bin/magpie-app"` and both entries stay launchable with the wrapper's environment; a Guix package points it at its launcher and the entry works instead of naming `ld-linux`.

**Verification.** `TestSetNamesThePackagersLauncher` and `TestRegisterSchemeNamesThePackagersLauncher` (wrapper path, and one with a space, asserting the quoted `Exec` and that the binary inside is not named) are red on clean main and green on the branch; `go test ./internal/autostart ./internal/gui -count=1` passes whole, `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go build` on both packages, and `GOOS=windows`/`GOOS=darwin` build and vet of `internal/autostart` (self() is shared). linux/amd64, go1.27.3.

**Boundary.** Not tried: a real NixOS `wrapGAppsHook` or Guix loader session launching the generated entry, and a real desktop parsing the quoted `Exec` (Edward4226 flagged the same gaps). The variable is used as written, relative or nonexistent included; validating the launcher stays the packager's job. magpie still writes its own entry into `$XDG_DATA_HOME` (it binds the window class and icon), so it still shadows a packaged entry in `XDG_DATA_DIRS` — but with `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` set the entry it writes is itself the working launcher. The generic no-registration gate suggested in the original report is not included; one knob covers both reported setups.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/1747-linux-guix-startup-writes-a

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.

### Conclusion

I published the `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` contract as a complete fork patch on current `origin/main` (`173b7e2742530dc6c9b7cd14f63cbf8eafc79f9c`). It names the launcher for both login autostart and the Linux desktop entry, without resolving a packager wrapper back to its inner binary.

### Evidence

- Branch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/tree/codex/issue-1747-packager-launcher
- Commit: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/commit/ca4f9b96bef9432e5bc62784ad8576ad2c061f36
- Patch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/commit/ca4f9b96bef9432e5bc62784ad8576ad2c061f36.patch
- Compare: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/compare/173b7e2742530dc6c9b7cd14f63cbf8eafc79f9c...codex/issue-1747-packager-launcher
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/autostart -run 'TestSelfUsesPackagerExecutable|TestSet$' -count=1`: pass
- Linux `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/autostart ./internal/gui` and Linux GUI test-binary compile: pass
- `gofmt`, `git diff --check`, Windows/Linux/macOS top-level builds: pass

The path used for `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` is quoted and escaped when it needs to be for the desktop entry's `Exec` key. This is an independent implementation of the same contract as skygunner's branch above; the two are interchangeable.

### Boundary

This is opt-in for packagers. Flatpak still wins, AppImage and the default `os.Executable()` paths remain intact, and `keepWebData()` is unchanged. The launcher string is used as written; validation belongs to the packager.

### Gap

Not tried: a real NixOS `wrapGAppsHook3` or Guix loader session, a real desktop parsing the generated `Exec`, and a file chooser launched from that entry.

### Action

Cherry-pick `ca4f9b96b`, or run:

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie.git codex/issue-1747-packager-launcher
git cherry-pick ca4f9b96bef9432e5bc62784ad8576ad2c061f36
```

Do not apply both implementations. The issue remains open for review.

### Conclusion

On 2026-11-10, the `MAGPIE_EXECUTABLE` contract was refreshed against `40118730018fe48db225f13ff56b8ec2f1d75fa4` (`v0.1.3585`), because the earlier branch no longer applies cleanly to current `origin/main`. The packager-supplied launcher is now used for both login autostart and the Linux desktop entry, without resolving a wrapper back to its inner binary.

### Evidence

- Branch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/tree/codex/issue-1747-packager-launcher-20261110
- Commit: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/commit/90e28987f
- Patch: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/commit/90e28987f.patch
- Compare: https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie/compare/40118730018fe48db225f13ff56b8ec2f1d75fa4...codex/issue-1747-packager-launcher-20261110

On clean `401187300`, `self()` returned the test executable instead of the packager's `/nix/store/example/bin/magpie app`. With the patch, the focused autostart test passed:

```text
ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/autostart 0.419s
```

The desktop entry also quotes a launcher path containing spaces and escapes the `Exec` key's special characters. Its regression assertion requires `Exec=` to begin a line, so indentation cannot produce an invalid key unnoticed. `gofmt`, `git diff --check`, Windows/Linux `go vet`, Linux `internal/gui` and `internal/autostart` test-binary compilation, and Windows/Linux/macOS top-level builds passed.

### Boundary

This is opt-in for packagers. Flatpak still wins, AppImage and default `os.Executable()` behavior remain unchanged, `keepWebData()` is untouched, and the launcher is used as written. Validation of the path remains the packager's responsibility; a literal `%` in the path is outside this change.

### Gap

Not tried: a real NixOS `wrapGAppsHook3` or Guix loader session, runtime execution of the Linux GUI regression test, a desktop environment parsing the generated `Exec`, and a file chooser launched through the entry.

### Action

This is an independent implementation of the same contract as skygunner's branch; the implementations are interchangeable and should not both be applied. Cherry-pick `90e28987f`, or run:

```sh
git fetch https://github.com/Edward4226/magpie.git codex/issue-1747-packager-launcher-20261110
git cherry-pick 90e28987f
```

No issue status change is requested.

issue.title: linux: the dock and app grid show a gear — the generated desktop entry has no StartupWMClass, and its Icon is never installed

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### What happens

Running the released Linux binary directly — `./magpie-linux-amd64`, no package,
no `install.sh` — the tray icon is right, but the **dock** and the **app grid
("Show Apps")** both show the generic gear placeholder.

Installed through `install.sh` instead, both are right. The difference is the
two things that script does and a bare run does not (see Cause).

### Cause

Two independent gaps, both on the bare-binary path.

**(1) App grid gear: `Icon=magpie` names an icon that is never installed.**

`internal/gui/scheme_linux.go`, `registerScheme()`, writes this entry on every
start:

```
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=magpie
Comment=Every agent's model. One place.
Exec=<exe> %u
Icon=magpie
Categories=Development;Utility;
MimeType=x-scheme-handler/magpie;
Terminal=false
```

but nothing ever puts `magpie.png` under
`~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/*/apps/`, so the theme lookup finds nothing and
the shell falls back to `application-x-executable` — the gear.

`install.sh` does install it (`site/public/install.sh:132-133`):

```sh
mkdir -p "$share/icons/hicolor/256x256/apps"
get -o "$share/icons/hicolor/256x256/apps/magpie.png" "$site/img/icon-256.png"
```

`registerScheme()` does not. The icon is already in the binary —
`internal/gui/app.go:43` `//go:embed icon.png` (plus `icon-1024.png`) — it is
only ever handed to the tray (`app.go:494`, `app.go:499`).

**(2) Dock gear: the entry has no `StartupWMClass`, and the window's `app_id`
is not `magpie`.**

Wails takes the Wayland surface `app_id` from `g_get_prgname()`
(`v3/pkg/application/application_linux_appid.go`):

```go
// GTK takes the Wayland surface app_id from g_get_prgname(), so a window is
// only matched with its .desktop file when the program name carries the
// application id as well.
func programName(options Options, appID string) string {
	if options.Linux.ProgramName != "" {
		return options.Linux.ProgramName
	}
	if options.Linux.ApplicationID != "" {
		return appID
	}
	return ""
}
```

magpie sets neither (`internal/gui/app.go:354`):

```go
Linux: application.LinuxOptions{DisableQuitOnLastWindowClosed: true},
```

so `g_set_prgname` is never called and `app_id` stays whatever GTK picked up
from the executable — its basename, `magpie-linux-amd64`.

GNOME matches a Wayland window to a desktop file by `app_id` ↔
`StartupWMClass`, then by lowercase `app_id` ↔ desktop file id.
`magpie-linux-amd64` matches neither `magpie.desktop` nor the (absent)
`StartupWMClass`, so no app is bound to the window and the shell draws the gear
again — this time in the dock.

`install.sh` does not hit this because it renames the binary
(`site/public/install.sh:129`):

```sh
install -m 755 "$tmp/$file" "$bin/magpie"
```

so `app_id` becomes `magpie`, which is the desktop file id.

macOS and Windows show the right icon from the same source tree because the
icon travels inside the artifact (`Magpie.app/Contents/Resources/icon.icns` +
`CFBundleIconFile`, and the `.ico` in the PE resources) and the platform binds
it by itself. On Linux the binding is external state that has to be installed.

Related: #2225 plans `build/linux/` (nfpm, a `.desktop` file and a 256px icon)
for deb/rpm; #1777 fixed the same class of bug on Windows; #1747 is about this
same generated entry on Guix.

### Fix

Give the Linux build a stable `ApplicationID` so `app_id` stops depending on
what the binary happens to be named, then finish the entry and install the icon
in the one place that already writes there.

```diff
 // internal/gui/app.go
-Linux: application.LinuxOptions{DisableQuitOnLastWindowClosed: true},
+Linux: application.LinuxOptions{
+	DisableQuitOnLastWindowClosed: true,
+	ApplicationID:                 "ai.usemagpie.app", // the id singleInstance() already uses
+},
```

```diff
 // internal/gui/scheme_linux.go
 Exec=` + exe + ` %u
 Icon=magpie
+StartupWMClass=ai.usemagpie.app
 Categories=Development;Utility;
```

and write the embedded icon into the theme the way `install.sh` does
(`~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/{48,128,256,512}x*/apps/magpie.png`, from the
`icon.png` / `icon-1024.png` already embedded).

`Icon=magpie` then resolves, and the dock has a `StartupWMClass` to bind to —
on a bare run and under a package alike, whatever the binary is named.

### Verification

On a bare run (Ubuntu, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland, `magpie-linux-amd64`):

- `~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/*/apps/magpie.png` — absent.
- `~/.local/share/applications/magpie.desktop` — no `StartupWMClass`.
- `Gtk.IconTheme` finds no `magpie` icon at any size.

The real `app_id` can be read on a Wayland session with:

```sh
gdbus call --session --dest org.gnome.Shell --object-path /org/gnome/Shell/Introspect \
  --method org.gnome.Shell.Introspect.GetWindows | tr '{' '\n' | grep app-id
```

### Environment

- Ubuntu, GNOME Shell 50.1, Wayland (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`)
- install: bare `magpie-linux-amd64` from the release, no package
- Wails `v3.0.0-beta.24`
